title: There seems / seem to be
titleZh: 「There seems / seem to be 句」表達「似乎有……」
titleEn: Using There seems / seem to be to express uncertain existence

source.file: Sentence Structure 170 -「There seems _ seem to be 句」表達「似乎有……」.pdf
omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.

formula: There seems to be + singular noun / uncountable noun + other information

formulas.formula: There seems to be + singular noun / uncountable noun + other information
There seem to be + plural noun + other information
There does not seem to be + singular noun / uncountable noun
There do not seem to be + plural noun
There seemed to be / did not seem to be + noun phrase

example: There seems to be a misunderstanding.

examples.en: There seems to be a misunderstanding.
examples.highlight: There seems to be a misunderstanding.

rules.zh: 單數或不可數名詞使用 seems （似乎有一個問題。） （似乎有些混亂。）
rules.en: Use seems with a singular countable noun or an uncountable noun: There seems to be a problem; There seems to be some confusion.
examples: There seems to be a problem.
There seems to be some confusion.

rules.zh: 複數名詞使用 seem （似乎有幾個錯誤。） 不可寫成：
rules.en: Use seem with a plural noun: There seem to be several mistakes, not There seems to be several mistakes.
examples: There seem to be several mistakes.

rules.zh: 否定句要使用 does not / do not + seem 單數或不可數名詞： （似乎沒有足夠時間。） 複數名詞： （似乎沒有任何巴士。） 使用 does、do 或 did 後，必須使用原形 seem，不可使用 seems 或 seemed。
rules.en: In negative sentences, use does not or do not + seem. Use There does not seem to be ... with a singular or uncountable noun, and There do not seem to be ... with a plural noun. After does, do or did, use the base form seem, never seems or seemed.
examples: There does not seem to be enough time.
There do not seem to be any buses.

rules.zh: 過去的情況使用 seemed （昨天似乎出現了問題。） 無論後面的名詞是單數還是複數，過去式均使用 seemed。
rules.en: Use seemed for a past situation, as in There seemed to be a problem yesterday. The past form is seemed whether the following noun is singular or plural.
examples: There seemed to be a problem yesterday.

rules.zh: There 在這個句型中不表示「那裏」 在 There seems to be a problem 中，There 只是用來開始存在句，並不表示某個地方。
rules.en: There does not mean “that place” in this structure. In There seems to be a problem, There merely begins an existential sentence.

rules.zh: to be 後面通常接名詞或名詞詞組 正確： 錯誤： 應改為：
rules.en: To be is normally followed by a noun or noun phrase, such as a problem, something wrong or several possible reasons.
examples: There seems to be a problem.
There seems to be something wrong.
There seem to be several possible reasons.

rules.zh: 不確定時才使用這個句型 如事情已經完全確定，通常直接使用 There is 或 There are。 確定： （廚房確實發生火警。） 未完全確定： （廚房似乎有東西正在燃燒。）
rules.en: Use this structure only when the information is uncertain. If something is fully established, normally use There is or There are. There is a fire in the kitchen makes a definite statement; There seems to be something burning in the kitchen reports an uncertain impression.
examples: There is a fire in the kitchen.
There seems to be something burning in the kitchen.

rules.zh: 本練習只訓練 seem There appears to be 也是正確英文，但本練習的答案必須使用：
rules.en: This exercise practises seem only. There appears to be is also grammatical English, but answers here must use one of the target forms: There seems/seem to be, There does/do not seem to be, or There seemed/did not seem to be.
examples: There seems to be
There seem to be
There does not seem to be
There do not seem to be
There seemed to be
There did not seem to be

benefits.zh: 避免把未確定的事情說成事實 當你只看到一些跡象，但仍未掌握所有資料時，這個句型可以讓你的說法更加準確。 直接斷定： （打印機有問題。） 較謹慎： （打印機似乎有問題。） 第二句表示你發現了一些問題跡象，但仍未完全確定原因。
benefits.en: It avoids presenting uncertain information as fact. When you have noticed signs but do not yet have all the information, the structure makes your statement more accurate. There is a problem with the printer is definite; There seems to be a problem with the printer is cautious and shows that you have noticed evidence of a problem without yet knowing the cause.
examples: There is a problem with the printer.
There seems to be a problem with the printer.

benefits.zh: 不需要反覆使用 “I think” 學生經常使用： 使用這個句型後，可以改為： 這樣可以把重點放在「問題」本身，而不是反覆強調「我認為」。
benefits.en: It avoids repeatedly using I think. I think there is a problem can become There seems to be a problem, keeping the focus on the possible problem rather than repeatedly emphasising the speaker's opinion.
examples: I think there is a problem.
There seems to be a problem.

benefits.zh: 適合指出問題、異常和疑問 這個句型特別適合用來談論： a problem 一個問題 a mistake 一個錯誤 a misunderstanding 一場誤會 some confusion 一些混亂 a delay 一次延誤 several possible causes 幾個可能成因 因此，它在日常對話、顧客服務、會議、報告和分析中都非常實用。
benefits.en: It is useful for identifying possible problems, mistakes, misunderstandings, confusion, delays and causes in conversation, service, meetings, reports and analysis.
examples: a problem
a mistake
a misunderstanding
some confusion
a delay
several possible causes

benefits.zh: 讓語氣更加客觀和有禮貌 直接說： （你犯了錯。） 有時可能顯得過於直接。 較中性的說法： （報告似乎有一個錯誤。） 這種說法把注意力放在事情上，而不是立即責怪某個人。
benefits.en: It makes the tone more objective and polite by focusing on the situation instead of immediately blaming a person.
examples: You made a mistake.
There seems to be a mistake in the report.

benefits.zh: 可以清楚表達現在、過去和否定情況 掌握這個句型後，你可以表達： （現在似乎有問題。） （當時似乎有問題。） （似乎沒有問題。） 同一個句型框架可以應付多種真實情況。
benefits.en: It clearly expresses present, past and negative possibilities in one flexible frame: There seems to be a problem; There seemed to be a problem; There does not seem to be a problem. The same structure therefore serves many real situations.
examples: There seems to be a problem.
There seemed to be a problem.
There does not seem to be a problem.
